text:
maya: Heads-up — we just noticed a canary we rolled for model-v3 caused a bunch of premium requests to fall back to model-v1-large. Cost spike and some SLA noise. Anyone seen similar?
vikram: I saw the metrics. Looks like the routing rule for the canary didn't include a per-tier fallback guard. So when the canary capacity was hit, smart-routing chose the nearest compatible variant which happened to be larger. :grimacing:
liz: Are you saying fallback ignored tier scoping? We intended canaries scoped to premium only and fallbacks to stay within that tier's allowed variants.
maya: Exactly. Canary config was: `scope: { tiers: ["premium"], regions: ["us-east-1"] }` but the runtime fallback logic only checked model compatibility + latency budget, not tier constraints.
tom: That's a bug imo — fallback should never escalate to a variant not allowed by the original scope. Either clamp fallback set to the scoped variant list or provide explicit 'allow_escalation: true/false' flag on the rollout record.
nana: +1 on a flag. Some customers might prefer the app to keep serving at higher cost vs returning 429. We need opt-in.
vikram: Implementation-wise we have two options: (1) enforce 'scope-hard' where fallback is filtered by scope, default for per-tier rollouts. (2) keep current soft-scope but expose `escalation` in rollout UI/API and default to false for paid tiers.
maya: For safety I'd prefer defaulting to hard-scope for any rollout tied to a tier or quota. That avoids surprise bill hits.
console-bot: quick note — console telemetry currently attributes tokens to the endpoint/model that actually served the request, but it doesn't reconcile origin rollout scope. We should add `rollout_id` and `rollout_scope` tags to serve events.
liz: Yes we need telemetry fields: `rollout_id`, `requested_scope.tiers`, `fallback_reason`, `final_variant`, `escalation_performed` so we can build a per-tier exposure/fallback dashboard.
tom: UX question — in the Console, should we show fallback counts as warnings on the rollout overview? Example: "2.3k fallbacks (escalation=1.1k)" with a link to sample traces.
maya: That would help CS teams. Also add a quota impact panel: "Tokens served under fallback vs expected" so finance can see delta.
vikram: On quota enforcement — when a fallback selects a variant outside a customer's reserved Dedicated pool, we currently try to route to hosted capacity. That broke assumptions for Dedicated customers who expect isolation. We need policy: if rollout scope includes dedicated_only=true, then fallback must also be dedicated-only or else fail open/closed behavior must be explicit.
nana: sounds right. For Dedicated we should default to fail-closed (i.e., reject) unless customer explicitly allows hosted fallback.
console-bot: suggestion: add two toggles in rollout modal: [x] scope to tiers/regions (checkboxes) and [ ] allow variant escalation (checkbox) + radio for fallback behavior: reject | route-hosted | route-compatible.
liz: API proposal (sketch):
```json
{
  "model": "model-v3",
  "rollout": {
    "id": "r-2026-03-18-01",
    "scope": { "tiers": ["premium"], "regions": ["us-east-1"] },
    "fallback_policy": "scoped-only", // options: scoped-only, allow-escalation, reject
    "allow_escalation": false
  }
}
```
vikram: I prefer explicit `fallback_policy` enum instead of mixing booleans. Simpler for runtime decision tree.
tom: We'll need unit tests covering: scoped fallback, escalation path, dedicated-only vs hosted fallbacks, and telemetry tags populated.
maya: Also add a migration plan: existing rollouts without policy should default to `allow-escalation` for free-tier and `scoped-only` for paid/dedicated. Document clearly in changelog.
vikram: I'll sketch runtime changes: when a route misses capacity, the router will compute candidate_variants = intersection(allowed_variants_by_scope, compatibility_set). If empty and fallback_policy==allow-escalation then compute compatibility_set only. Emit `escalation_performed=true` if final_variant not in allowed_variants_by_scope.
nana: Can we also track latency delta when fallback occurs? We saw some requests that had much larger p95 when they hit the hosted fallback.
liz: Telemetry should include `latency_before_fallback` (if we detect pre-fallback attempt) and `latency_after_fallback`. At minimum we can tag the event with `fallback_latency_delta_ms`.
deploy-bot: deploy started: rollout-service v2.14.0 -> staging at 1834567920
maya: Action items: (1) Vikram implement `fallback_policy` enum + router changes (2) Liz wire telemetry fields + console indicators (3) Tom add tests + dedicated policy enforcement (4) Ana update docs/changelog + migration decisions.
vikram: I'll own the router PR, target EOD tomorrow for initial tests.
liz: I'll add telemetry schema and a mock dashboard to staging.
tom: Tests — I'll add integration tests and a small harness to simulate per-tier saturation.
nana: Docs note — I'll write the rollout behavior section and update default semantics for dedicated customers.
maya: Thanks all. If anyone sees urgent customer impact today ping me and I'll pause canary exposures for premium tiers. :pray:
vikram: pinged @maya if we should auto-pause exposures when escalation rate > 5% in 5m window? Could add as a circuit-breaker policy.
maya: Good idea. Add as optional auto-pause guard.
console-bot: rollout-service v2.14.0 deployed to staging at 1834568025
maya: closing loop for now. Will follow up in docs PR.
